title: In Mid-Year Global Outlook, JPMorgan Raises Year-End S&P 500 - The Wealth Advisor
text: JPMorgan has raised its year-end S&P 500 target to 7,800, citing accelerating AI-driven growth, improving earnings expectations, and a more constructive geopolitical backdrop. For wealth advisors and RIAs, the firm's updated outlook reinforces the case for maintaining strategic equity exposure while preparing clients for heightened market volatility along the way. In its mid-year global outlook, JPMorgan noted that easing tensions between the United States and Iran are bringing markets closer to its “Blue Sky” scenario, prompting an increase in its S&P 500 target from 7,600 to 7,800. The revised forecast implies approximately 6% upside from recent levels, although strategists caution that the path forward is unlikely to be smooth. The firm expects the Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged through 2026, with the possibility of rate increases emerging in 2027. Against this backdrop, market leadership is expected to remain concentrated among large-cap Quality Growth companies and businesses with direct exposure to artificial intelligence. While the long-term outlook remains constructive, JPMorgan warns that speculative activity in secondary AI-related stocks has reached elevated levels. The firm believes excessive momentum-driven trading has increased the probability of a sharp market dislocation or “flash crash,” characterized by a rapid decline in asset prices followed by a swift recovery. Advisors should be prepared for periods of volatility, particularly within crowded segments of the AI ecosystem. Despite these risks, JPMorgan maintains that underlying fundamentals remain favorable and suggests investors view market pullbacks as potential opportunities rather than reasons to reduce exposure. The firm’s conviction is supported by a significant upward revision to its 2026 S&P 500 earnings-per-share forecast, now projected at $350, representing a 29% year-over-year increase. The earnings upgrade reflects an unprecedented pace of positive earnings revisions and a substantial increase in AI-related capital expenditures among major technology companies. Continued investment in AI infrastructure is expected to support revenue growth, productivity gains, and broader corporate profitability across multiple sectors. On the consumer front, JPMorgan’s credit card spending data suggests household finances remain resilient. However, management commentary across industries points to a more selective and value-conscious consumer environment, indicating strength is not evenly distributed across income cohorts or spending categories. The S&P 500 has gained nearly 8% year to date and approximately 16% since its late-March lows. Much of that performance has been driven by the Technology sector, which has advanced roughly 27% this year, led by strong gains in semiconductor companies. For advisors, the key challenge will be balancing participation in AI-driven growth opportunities while managing concentration risk and client expectations around inevitable periods of market turbulence.
